title: Melodia Model Tier Registry
purpose: Machine-readable tier policy that tells an autonomous agent fleet WHICH class of model a task packet may use, so frontier spend lands on architectural decisions and cheap/free models carry the easy work. This registry selects models; it never becomes a second orchestrator, router or lease framework.

rules.deterministic: Routing is a pure function of the packet plus this registry. No randomness, no model voting, no free-form judgement.
rules.extend_not_replace: Extend Tools/model_router.py. No second router, orchestrator, lease or lane framework may be created.
rules.no_self_certification: The tier that produced an artifact never accepts it. Acceptance is T1_VERIFIER or a human/gate script.
rules.no_silent_paid_fallback: A local-only or bulk lane must fail loudly rather than reach a paid endpoint.
rules.one_editor_writer: A stronger model does not relax the single-editor / single-mutation-surface rule; editor mutation needs the lease.
rules.delegated_output_is_not_evidence: A report is not evidence; the verifier opens the artifact (AGENTS.md binding rule).
rules.widest_tier_wins: When a packet matches several escalation triggers, the most restrictive (highest) tier wins.
rules.demote_after_proof: A repeated task shape that clears promotion_evidence at the same tier three times may be re-tiered one step cheaper by an owner-reviewed registry edit.

escalation_triggers.why: Module/Build.cs/uproject/plugin changes are architectural: they alter the reflected build graph for everyone.
The CLAUDE.md never-touch table is owner-sign-off only, enforced by .githooks/pre-commit (SKIP_PROTECTION).
Save format, USTRUCT layout and restore semantics are runtime compatibility contracts (Issue #51 class).
A new/renamed public subsystem, interface or base class is an architecture decision with downstream owners.
Schemas and v1 contracts are consumed by compilers, drivers and gates; a silent edit breaks producers.
L_SakuraPath / L_MelusinaMorning composition and Content/_PROJECT are ask-first owner surfaces.
Git pipeline law: no branch/commit/merge/rebase/reset/push and no p4 submit without explicit owner permission.
Secrets never enter Git; provider keys live in env or ~/.hermes.
Editor mutation is lease-gated and must be verified by opening the artifact; it is never a swarm lane.
Any artifact claimed as evidence needs a verifier that is not its producer.

cheap_tier_eligible.why: Documentation prose, fold-in edits and link repair are reviewable by diff and cheap to redo.
Reading a long log and citing lines is bounded, verifiable and does not mutate the engine.
Manifests, indexes and dataset rows are data edits under an existing schema.
Fixture data and expected-output files sit behind a contract test that fails on a wrong edit.
A tool with an existing offline contract test may be extended by a cheap lane; the test is the guard rail.

tiers.label: Frontier architect
tiers.intent: Make and record the architectural decision: module graph, persistence format, public owner surface, contract/schema, migration or convergence strategy. Produce a decision spec (ADR) the cheaper tiers then execute mechanically.
must_not: accept its own artifact as evidence
land a git or p4 operation without explicit owner permission
invent a second world/save/routing/orchestration authority
write Content/** binaries or Config/** directly

include: the named owner files for the decision

tiers.handoff: A written decision spec naming the exact files, the owner it extends, the must-not list and the acceptance check. Cheap tiers execute it; they never re-decide it.

tiers.label: Independent verifier
tiers.intent: Open the artifact and try to falsify it. Fresh eyes on someone else's output, or on a frontier decision before it becomes law.
must_not: be the producer of the artifact it grades
record a gate pass where a human or gate script is required
soften a failure into a success
tiers.handoff: A receipt naming what was opened, what was measured, pass/fail and the residual uncertainty. Never a prose summary of the producer's report.

tiers.label: Bounded executor
tiers.intent: Implement an already-decided change inside a declared write fence: tools, harness fixes, C++ touching one named owner, tests, offline scripts.
must_not: change the module graph, Build.cs or .uproject
re-open a decided architecture
write Content/** binaries, Config/** or the never-touch table
edit CURRENT_STATE.md

include: the existing test for the touched tool

tiers.handoff: A patch plus the exact command and its raw output. No narrative claim beyond the log.

tiers.label: Bulk / easy work
tiers.intent: The 80% that is not a decision: docs prose, log triage, manifests, indexes, fixtures, dataset rows, summarizing a long file, mechanical refactors guarded by an existing test.
must_not: write Source/**
touch Config/**, .uproject, Build.cs or the never-touch table
edit CURRENT_STATE.md
change a schema, contract or public API
accept its own artifact

include: the citation list, not the repo
the cheap_tier_eligible entry that authorises it

evidence.verified_by: T1_VERIFIER or the existing contract test

tiers.handoff: A diff whose every claim cites a file and line, or an artifact path the verifier can open. Cheap lanes must be reversible.

tiers.label: Local / free daemon
tiers.intent: Zero-cost volume and unattended work: overnight daemons, drafts, production-lane content that is gate-accepted, offline sweeps. Local-first so production content never needs the network.
must_not: reach a paid cloud endpoint (no silent bill)
record a ledger pass for its own output
write Content/** binaries or Config/**
take the editor lock unattended
tiers.handoff: An artifact plus an offline probe result. A local lane never closes a gate on its own word.

architecture_decision.rationale: Cross-subsystem contracts, public API mutations, boundary governance. Requires maximal reasoning depth and non-hallucinatory invariant adherence.

cpp_core_implementation.rationale: High-depth C++ UE idioms, macro awareness (UPROPERTY/UFUNCTION), pointer safety, engine lifecycle hooks.

shader_hlsl_rendering.rationale: HLSL, Substrate slabs, Nanite custom depth, Niagara render modules, post-process material passes.

ui_widget_implementation.rationale: Slate/UMG widget layout hierarchies, event-driven binding, responsive container anchors.

test_generation.rationale: Headless contract test fixtures, assertion coverage, parametrization of input cases.

doc_indexing_synthesis.rationale: Massive context ingestion, rapid documentation indexing, doc frontmatter alignment, cross-file bibliography synthesis.

git_vcs_automation.rationale: Local-only, zero-cost commit message generation, pre-commit linting, status checks, branch health verification.

atlas_validation.rationale: Strict Python schema validation, disk-state integrity checks, zero-hallucination deterministic script enforcement.
